Prediction target period: from 2025-07-08 to 2025-07-23. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> On July 1, 2025, the Ghana Cocoa Board (Cocobod) projected the country's cocoa crop for the 2025/26 season to be 650,000 metric tons. This forecast represents an 8.3% increase from the estimated 600,000 metric tons anticipated for the 2024/25 season. The projection was reported on July 2, 2025. <2> On June 27, 2025, Innova Market Insights released its 'Top Trends 2025: Chocolate Confectionery' global report, detailing key shifts in consumer preferences. The report identifies a strong consumer desire for inventive flavors and surprising combinations that create "wow" moments and extraordinary experiences. Another major trend is the increasing demand for products addressing digestive and gut health, which has become a primary driver for functional food purchases. The analysis also highlights a focus on multi-sensorial experiences to create new forms of indulgence and confirms the success of limited-edition products, which show sustained year-over-year growth in new launches. <3> The International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) released its market report covering May 2025 on June 12, 2025. The report indicated that cocoa futures prices experienced both bullish and bearish pressures throughout May. A key bullish factor was a shift in market focus from the volume of cocoa to its quality. On the bearish side, influencing factors included improved weather conditions and reduced concerns over the levels of cocoa inventory. <4> In late May 2025, an Elliott Wave technical analysis indicated that cocoa futures were in a sharp decline, continuing a bearish trend that commenced on December 18, 2024. [1, 2] According to the analysis, a corrective zigzag formation, identified as wave ((B)), which started in April 2025, reached its conclusion on May 20, 2025. [1] Following the end of this corrective wave, the price was projected to move lower in a new five-wave sequence. [1] Analysts predicted this downward movement could break below the low set in April 2025, with potential target support zones between 5980 to 3952 and 6576 to 5356. [1, 2] <5> The International Cocoa Organization's market report for April 2025 indicated that cocoa prices were initially supported by news of a potentially poor mid-crop from West Africa. [2, 3] However, the announcement of a 10% U.S. import tariff caused prices to drop significantly mid-month, with a 17% fall in London and 16% in New York. [3] Prices later recovered in the third week following a temporary pause in the imposition of some tariffs and were further boosted by better-than-expected first-quarter grinding data. [3] Although the quarterly grindings were negative, they signaled some demand resilience, contributing to the price rebound. [2, 3] <6> Concerns over the development of Côte d'Ivoire's April-to-September cocoa mid-crop emerged due to fluctuating and extreme weather patterns in 2025, which contributed to price rallies. While farmers initially expressed concern in April over below-average rainfall and heat, heavy and above-average rains at the end of April and into June led to a revised outlook, with some fearing flooding and disease while others anticipated a boost to the crop's later stages. [5, 2, 9] [6, 11] Reports indicated that the inconsistent rainfall negatively impacted the quality of the mid-crop beans. [7, 8] This ongoing weather volatility in the world's top cocoa producer has been a significant factor supporting higher cocoa prices throughout the season. [3, 4] <7> In May 2025, the 17th edition of the "State of the Industry: Chocolate Candy in the U.S." report was published, offering a detailed analysis of the U.S. chocolate candy market. This comprehensive annual report examines historical, current, and projected trends from 2010 to 2029. Key areas covered include in-depth data on sales, consumption patterns, pricing fluctuations, and raw material trends, which are significantly influenced by cocoa prices. The report also provides a breakdown of market shares for leading brands in the dark, milk, and white chocolate sectors, along with dollar and unit sales for the top 10 producers. Furthermore, it delves into key industry developments such as the growing popularity of premium, dark, functional, and plant-based chocolates, as well as the rise of organic options and the importance of sustainability. <8> In late April 2025, market analysis confirmed that cocoa futures were climbing again following a significant drop in March to around $8,000 per tonne from winter highs that exceeded $12,500 per tonne. The resurgence was attributed to two primary factors: persistent supply concerns in West Africa and unexpectedly resilient global demand. The outlook for the mid-crop harvest in Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana, which together produce over 60% of the world's cocoa, was described as bleak due to unfavorable weather, aging trees, and economic pressures on farmers. Concurrently, demand from North America, Europe, and Asia proved stronger than anticipated. For instance, Q1 European cocoa grindings fell by only 3.7% and Asian grindings by 3.4%, both smaller declines than the forecasted 5% drop. This indicated robust demand, further bolstered by a growing appetite for premium chocolate in established markets and rising consumption in emerging economies like India and China. A flat 10% tariff rate on U.S. imports also provided some support for prices. <9> Throughout March 2025, the U.S. cocoa market experienced significant uncertainty due to the anticipation of universal tariffs on cocoa imports. [5, 17] Although the tariffs had not yet been implemented during that month, their prospect contributed to market jitters as participants feared potential impacts on global trade and increased economic uncertainty. [5, 17] <10> A report released on April 11, 2025, by the Energy & Climate Intelligence Unit (ECIU) detailed the significant impact of climate change on cocoa production. The analysis identified extreme weather events in West Africa as a primary cause of price instability, noting that cocoa prices had more than tripled compared to April 2022. The report emphasized that the already high temperatures and changing precipitation patterns in these regions make them exceptionally vulnerable to the effects of climate change.
